extracted.intended_audience: ORR staff, contracted care provider facilities, legal service providers, child advocates, and other stakeholders involved in care of unaccompanied children
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory standards and operational requirements governing the care, medical treatment, legal services, placement, transportation, transfers, age determinations, data reporting, emergency/influx operations, and protections for unaccompanied children in ORR custody.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical isolation allowed only as necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: An unaccompanied child may be placed in medical isolation and excluded from contact with the general population to prevent spread of infectious disease, protect other children and staff, or as required under State/local/licensing rules, but such isolation must be limited only to the extent necessary to ensure health and welfare.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Medically isolated children must still receive mandated services to the greatest extent practicable, be supervised under applicable licensing ratios, and, if multiple children are isolated, should be placed together as practicable given the nature of the medical issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial placement considers individualized medical needs
rubrics_metrics.description: When placing an unaccompanied child, ORR considers the child's individualized needs and any specialized services or treatment required or reasonably requested, including access to medical specialists, family planning, and services requiring heightened ORR involvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If medically necessary care is identified at referral, intake, Initial Medical Exam, or at any point in custody (or requested), ORR shall, to the greatest extent possible, identify available appropriate bed space and place the child at a facility able to provide or arrange such care, in an appropriate location, with access to an appropriate medical provider.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfers for medical care when appropriate placement unavailable
rubrics_metrics.description: If an appropriate initial placement is not immediately available or medical needs are identified after the Initial Medical Exam, care providers must immediately notify ORR and ORR shall, to the greatest extent possible, transfer the child to a program meeting the required qualifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies whenever care is medically necessary and not available at current placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure transportation/access to medical care across state lines
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR shall ensure unaccompanied children have access to medical care, including transportation across State lines and associated ancillary services if necessary to access appropriate medical services, including specialists and services requiring heightened ORR involvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirement applies regardless of whether Federal appropriations law prevents ORR from paying for the medical care itself. If conflicts with State law arise, ORR will review circumstances to ensure statutory responsibilities are met; Federal duties govern ORR employees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt notification to ORR of heightened medical needs or pregnancy
rubrics_metrics.description: Care provider facilities shall notify ORR within 24 hours of a child's need or request for medical services requiring heightened ORR involvement or the discovery of a pregnancy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Child advocates make independent best interest recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Child advocates are third parties who make independent recommendations regarding the best interests of an unaccompanied child based on information from the child and other sources; recommendations (Best Interest Determinations, BIDs) may be submitted to ORR and/or immigration court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sources for recommendations can include parents, family, sponsors, government agencies, legal providers, care provider representatives, health professionals, and others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Child advocate responsibilities (visitation, explanation, advocacy, BIDs, communication)
rubrics_metrics.description: Child advocates' responsibilities include: visiting clients; explaining consequences and potential outcomes of decisions affecting the child; advocating for the child's best interest regarding care, placement, services, release, and proceedings; providing BIDs where appropriate and within a reasonable time; and regularly communicating case updates with care provider, ORR, and other stakeholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocacy includes updates related to services provided after release from ORR care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment criteria and process for child advocates
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR may appoint child advocates for trafficking victims and especially vulnerable children. Interested parties may refer children to ORR for an advocate. ORR shall make an appointment decision within five business days of a referral except under exceptional circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR will appoint advocates for children currently or previously in ORR care; does not appoint for children never in ORR care. "Interested parties" includes ORR staff, immigration judge, DHS staff, legal service providers, care providers, healthcare professionals, child advocate organizations, etc. Child advocate appointments terminate upon case closure by advocate, child's 18th birthday, or when child obtains lawful immigration status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Child advocates' access to clients and case files
rubrics_metrics.description: After appointment, child advocates shall be provided access to their clients during normal business hours at an ORR care provider facility and access to all their client's case file information, and may request copies of the case file directly from the care provider without using ORR's standard case file request process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality obligations for child advocates
rubrics_metrics.description: Child advocates must keep case file information and information about the child's case confidential and shall not disclose case file information except to ORR grantees, contractors, and Federal staff. They shall not disclose information to other parties with an interest in the child's case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR shall allow child advocates to conduct private communications with the child in a private area that allows confidentiality for in-person and virtual/telephone meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-retaliation for child advocates
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR shall presume child advocates act in good faith and shall not retaliate against a child advocate for actions taken within the scope of their responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: ORR shall not retaliate due to disagreement with a BID or because of advocacy on behalf of a child.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orientation legal presentation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An unaccompanied child shall receive an in-person, telephonic, or video presentation concerning the rights and responsibilities of undocumented children in the immigration system, presented in the child's language and in an age-appropriate manner, provided by an independent legal service provider with appropriate qualifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presentation must include legal rights and responsibilities, protections under child labor laws, services entitled (including education), be delivered in the child's language and age-appropriate, occur within 10 business days of admission and transfer (with exceptions), and every 6 months for unrepresented children remaining in custody; if released before 10 days, follow up to complete presentation as soon as practicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inform unaccompanied children about free legal assistance and representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Children must be informed about availability of free legal assistance and that they may be represented by counsel at no expense to the government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notify children of immigration relief options and rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Children must be notified of ability to petition for SIJ classification, request juvenile court determinations per §410.1209, apply for asylum or other relief from removal, right to a removal hearing before an immigration judge, ability to apply for asylum with USCIS first, and ability to request voluntary departure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential legal consultation within 10 business days
rubrics_metrics.description: An unaccompanied child shall receive a confidential legal consultation with a qualified attorney (or supervised paralegal/EOIR representative) to determine possible forms of relief from removal and other case disposition options, occurring within 10 business days of transfer to a new ORR facility or upon request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR shall request an additional legal consultation on behalf of a child identified as (A) potential trafficking victim, (B) abused/abandoned/neglected, (C) victim of crime/domestic violence, or (D) persecuted or fearing persecution for protected grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Private communications with legal representative
rubrics_metrics.description: A child in ORR care shall be able to conduct private communications with their attorney of record, EOIR accredited representative, or legal service provider in a private enclosed area that allows confidentiality for in-person, virtual, or telephone meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility and posting of legal information
rubrics_metrics.description: Information required for orienting and informing children of legal rights and access to services must be posted in an age-appropriate format and translated into each child's preferred language in any ORR contracted or grant-funded facility where children are in ORR care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct immigration representation funding criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: To the extent appropriations are available and pro bono counsel is impracticable, ORR shall fund legal service providers to provide direct immigration legal representation for certain children, at ORR's discretion and subject to available appropriations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include: unrepresented children enrolled in URM programs (if still under 18 and without relief), children in EOIR proceedings where other assistance insufficient, children released to sponsors in the same service area as the legal provider who assisted in ORR care (to promote continuity), and other children as ORR determines funding allows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding for legal services in non-immigration matters
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR may fund access to counsel for non-immigration matters to ensure children's interests are considered in matters relating to care and custody, subject to availability of appropriations and ORR discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerated matters include ORR appellate procedures (Placement Review Panel, risk determination hearings), children placed in long-term home care or RTC outside licensed facility when other assistance insufficient, children with no identified sponsor unable to be placed in long-term/transitional home care, judicial bypass to access lawful medical procedures requiring parental consent, representation in state juvenile court when child has SIJ, and assistance obtaining employment authorization documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for legal services delivery
rubrics_metrics.description: In-person meetings are preferred during legal counsel provision though telephonic/teleconference may substitute as appropriate. Either the child's attorney, EOIR accredited representative, or a care provider staff member shall always accompany the child to any in-person courtroom hearing or proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon receipt of proof of representation and signed authorization, ORR shall share, upon request, the child's complete case file apart from legally required redactions to assist in legal representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants/contracts to legal service providers
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR may make discretionary grants or contracts to qualified agencies/organizations to ensure access to immigration legal representation, assistance and related services to children in ORR care or released and living in a State/region, in accordance with authorizing statutes and eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants/contracts subject to available resources; formula grants can be geographically distributed proportional to population of released children; grants calculated based on historic proportion of child population in State within a lookback period determined annually by the Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-retaliation against legal service providers
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR shall presume legal service providers are acting in good faith and shall not retaliate against them for actions taken within their responsibilities, including reporting harm or misconduct on behalf of a child.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informed consent and oversight for psychotropic medications
rubrics_metrics.description: Except in a psychiatric emergency, ORR shall ensure that, whenever possible, authorized individuals provide informed consent prior to administration of psychotropic medications to unaccompanied children. ORR must ensure meaningful oversight of administration of psychotropic medication(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Section 504 protections to children with disabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR must provide notice to children in its custody of protections against discrimination under Section 504 (45 CFR part 85) and notice of procedures for seeking reasonable modifications or making complaints about alleged discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Most integrated setting requirement for children with disabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR shall administer the UC Program in the most integrated setting appropriate to the needs of unaccompanied children with disabilities in accordance with 45 CFR 85.21(d), unless ORR can demonstrate that doing so would fundamentally alter the nature of its UC Program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide reasonable modifications for equal access
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR shall provide reasonable modifications needed for a child with one or more disabilities to have equal access to the UC Program, but is not required to take action that would result in a fundamental alteration in nature of a program or activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where applicable, ORR shall document in the child's case file any services, supports, or program modifications provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor assessment and PRS considerations for children with disabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR's assessment of a potential sponsor's capability to provide for a child's physical and mental well-being must include explicit consideration of the impact of the child's disability. In PRS, ORR and entities providing PRS must make reasonable modifications to enable released children with disabilities to live in the most integrated setting appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR will assist otherwise viable sponsors in accessing and coordinating appropriate post-release community-based services; ORR shall not delay release solely because post-release services are not in place before release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transport appropriate to age and needs; timely release transportation assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Care provider facilities shall transport a child in a manner appropriate to the child's age and physical and mental needs (including proper use of car seats) and consistent with §410.1304. When ORR plans to release a child to a sponsor, ORR assists without undue delay in making transportation arrangements and may request the care provider facility to transport, reimburse, or directly pay for transportation as appropriate to facilitate timely release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Care provider facility must comply with relevant State/local licensing requirements and State/Federal regulations regarding transportation of children (e.g., staff/child ratio, vehicle maintenance/inspection).

rubrics_metrics.name: Background checks for drivers and gender assignment of transport staff
rubrics_metrics.description: Care provider facilities shall conduct all necessary background checks for drivers transporting children in compliance with §410.1305(a). If transporting, assign at least one transport staff of the same gender as the child being transported to the greatest extent possible under the circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data reporting requirements for care provider facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Care provider facilities are required to report information necessary for ORR to maintain data, including biographical information, date child entered Federal custody, placement/removal/release information, explanations for detention or release, disposition of actions involving the child, information from assessments/evaluations/reports, and data necessary to evaluate and improve care and services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR coordinates with other Departments to obtain some statistical data and obtains additional data from care provider facilities so ORR may compile and maintain statistical information on unaccompanied children.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuous assessment and least restrictive placement for transfers
rubrics_metrics.description: Care provider facilities shall continuously assess children to review whether placements are appropriate. A child shall be placed in the least restrictive setting that is in the best interests of the child, subject to considerations regarding danger to self/community and runaway risk. Care providers shall follow ORR guidance when making transfer recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an alternate placement better meets the child's needs, the care provider shall recommend transfer to ORR for approval within three business days of identifying the need.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical clearance and review timeframe for transfers
rubrics_metrics.description: The care provider must ensure the child is medically cleared for transfer within three business days of ORR identifying the need for transfer, unless waived by ORR. For children with acute/chronic conditions or seeking services requiring heightened involvement, care provider staff and ORR shall meet to review the transfer recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not medically cleared within three business days, care provider shall notify ORR; ORR will review and determine fitness for travel and, if denying transfer, shall notify and specify timeframe for reevaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance notice to interested parties prior to transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 48 hours prior to physical transfer, the referring care provider shall notify all appropriate interested parties (attorney of record/EOIR representative, legal service provider, child advocate) of the transfer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advance notice not required in unusual and compelling circumstances (e.g., safety threats, runaway risk, or waiver) in which case notice shall be provided within 24 hours following transfer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Items to accompany a child upon transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: A child shall be transferred with the child's possessions and legal papers, including personal belongings, the transfer request and tracking form, a 30-day medication supply if applicable, all health records, and original documents (including birth certificates).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If possessions exceed carrier limits, the care provider shall ship possessions to the child's subsequent placement in a timely manner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictive placement and transfer review every 30 days
rubrics_metrics.description: When a child is placed in a restrictive setting (secure, heightened supervision, or RTC), the care provider and ORR shall review the placement at least every 30 days to determine whether a new level of care is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If continued restrictive placement is appropriate, the care provider shall document the basis for the determination and, upon request, provide documentation of the review and rationale to the child's attorney, legal provider, and/or child advocate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group transfers and ORR guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: If circumstances require transferring more than one child at a time (e.g., emergencies, natural disasters, program closures, bed constraints), the care provider shall follow ORR guidance and the general transfer requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Residential treatment center (RTC) transfer procedures and review
rubrics_metrics.description: A care provider may request ORR transfer a child to an RTC pursuant to §410.1105(c). Placement of a child into an RTC shall be reviewed every 30 days in accordance with restrictive placement review requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency placement changes and notification timeframe
rubrics_metrics.description: In an emergency, a care provider facility may temporarily change the physical placement of a child prior to securing ORR permission but shall notify ORR of the change as soon as possible and in all cases within eight hours of transfer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age determinations use totality of circumstances and multiple evidence sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for determining age must take into account the totality of the circumstances and evidence, including non-exclusive use of radiographs. ORR may require medical or dental examinations (including X-rays) or other appropriate procedures to verify age. Determinations are made based on the totality of evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If ORR determines the individual is an unaccompanied child, they will be treated according to UC Program regulations for all purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enumerated evidence for age determinations and medical assessment threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR may consider: original or authentic birth certificates (or consulting consulate/embassy), authentic government-issued documents, baptismal/school/medical records, sworn affidavits from relatives, statements by the individual, statements from parents/legal guardians, statements from others apprehended with the individual, and medical age assessments (not sole determinant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a medical age assessment estimates a 75% or greater probability that the individual is 18 or older, and the totality of evidence indicates they are 18 or older, ORR must determine the individual is 18 or older. The 75% threshold applies to all medical methods identified as appropriate by medical community. Ambiguous or borderline forensic results resolved in favor of finding the individual is a minor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment when individual appears to be an adult
rubrics_metrics.description: If procedures would lead a reasonable person to conclude an individual is an adult despite the individual's claim to be under 18, ORR shall treat such person as an adult for all purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contingency planning and placement reassessment during emergencies/influxes
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR regularly reevaluates number of placements needed to determine whether shelters, heightened supervision facilities, and transitional home beds should be adjusted to accommodate changes in eligible unaccompanied children population. In events preventing prompt placement, ORR shall make all reasonable efforts to place each child in a standard program as expeditiously as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR implements contingency plans that may include opening facilities and prioritizing placement of certain children; continually develops standard programs available for emergency placements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain list of children affected during influx/emergency
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR maintains a list of unaccompanied children affected by emergency or influx including each child's name; date and country of birth; date of placement in ORR custody; and place and date of current placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum standards for emergency or influx facilities (basic care, medical, assessment, education, recreation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Emergency/influx facilities must provide proper physical care (suitable living accommodations, food, clothing, grooming items); appropriate routine medical and dental care including complete medical exam within 48 hours of admission (excluding weekends/holidays) unless recently examined at another ORR facility; immunizations per ACIP schedule; administration of prescribed medication and special diets; and appropriate mental health interventions when necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilities must provide an individualized needs assessment (initial intake forms, identification/history, special needs requiring immediate intervention, educational assessment/plan, family relationships assessment, religious preference, personal goals/strengths/weaknesses, identifying family members in the U.S.). Educational services must be in a structured classroom setting Monday–Friday focusing primarily on basic academic competencies and secondarily on English acquisition, include instruction/materials in needed languages and provide reading materials in other languages for leisure. Activities must include daily outdoor activity (weather permitting) with at least one hour/day of large muscle activity and one hour/day structured leisure activities (not TV).
